body.content: If we consider the 'Boeing 737 MAX' case (SCR_006), the failure wasn't a lack of checklists, but a failure of the 'expert' to communicate a hidden dependency. This suggests that the 'reliability' of a checklist panel is bounded by the 'completeness' of the checklist. If the checklist is 99% complete, the panel wins. If it's 80% complete, the expert's intuition (which captures the remaining 20%) is the only thing that prevents catastrophe.
body.why_keep_this: Explores the boundary condition of checklist completeness vs. expert intuition.
